landing.whyTitle: A Quran learning platform for memorizing, understanding and reciting
landing.whyP1: Quran Masterclass combines verse-by-verse audio from renowned reciters with word-by-word meaning, transliteration and classical tafsir. You hear a verse, see every word light up, and read what it means and what scholars explained about it – all on one screen, on your phone or computer.
landing.whyP2: Whether you want to memorize the Quran (hifz), understand its meaning (fahm) or improve your recitation (tilawa and tajweed), the app adapts: hide words and recite from memory, repeat verses or whole passages, and let spaced repetition show you what to review today. A kids mode makes learning simple and fun for children.
landing.q1: How can I memorize the Quran with Quran Masterclass?
landing.a1: Listen to a verse, then switch on “Hide half” or “Hide all” and recite it from memory. Reveal the verse and rate how well you knew it. The app schedules your next review after 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and 90 days, so verses move into long-term memory.
landing.q2: Which languages and translations are available?
landing.a2: The interface and the Quran translation are available in German, English, Arabic, French, Spanish, Chinese, Indonesian and Persian. Transliteration in Latin letters helps you read the Arabic text.
landing.q3: Is there a tafsir (Quran commentary) for every verse?
landing.a3: Classical commentaries such as Ibn Kathir (abridged) are shown next to the verse with their source. Where no tafsir exists in your language, English sources are shown instead.
landing.a4: Yes. You can listen, read and memorize for free. A free account saves your progress, bookmarks and review plan on all your devices. Visitors without an account can open tafsir for a limited number of verses per day.
landing.q5: Is there a mode for children?
landing.a5: Yes. Kids mode uses large text, bright colors, simple buttons and star rewards, so children can listen, follow word by word and practise short surahs.

home2.pathsTitle: Three ways to learn – one platform
home2.pathsIntro: Choose what matters to you today. You can switch at any time; your progress stays.
home2.pHifzD: Build a daily memorization routine: listen, read along, hide words, recite from memory and review at the right time. The review schedule brings every verse back before you forget it.
home2.pFahmD: Read the meaning of every word, follow the transliteration and open the tafsir next to the verse. Understanding makes memorizing easier and lasts longer.
home2.pTilawaD: Listen to renowned reciters verse by verse at your own speed, repeat difficult passages and follow every word as it is recited.
home2.methodIntro: Traditional hifz teachers work with three portions every day. Quran Masterclass follows the same structure:
home2.mNewD: A few verses you learn today: listen several times, read along, then hide the words.
home2.mRecentD: The portion of the last days. A short daily repetition keeps it fresh.
home2.mOldD: Everything you learned before, repeated in rotation so that nothing fades.
home2.methodOutro: The spaced-repetition schedule (after 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and 90 days) decides when each verse returns – you only practise what needs it.
home2.f7d: Save verses, write your own reflections and find them again on every device.
home2.f8d: Switch between verse cards and a continuous reading view with verse markers, page, juz and hizb.
home2.f9d: Find any verse by a word – in Arabic or in the language you read.
home2.mapBody: Every surah is a box that shows how well you know it: green sits firmly, gold is wobbling, red is difficult. Tap a surah to see every verse – and know exactly what to review next.

home2.pop4d: A surah of repeated reminders of divine mercy.

home2.tajBody: Good recitation starts with listening. Compare reciters, slow the audio down, repeat a verse as often as you need and follow every word as it is recited. Tajweed colors and rule explanations are being added step by step.

home2.langsBody: Quran Masterclass speaks {n} languages – from Arabic, Urdu, Turkish and Persian to Pashto, Bengali, Indonesian, German, French, Spanish, Russian and Chinese. Whether you live in Pakistan, Afghanistan, Turkey, Egypt, Indonesia, Bangladesh, Germany or anywhere else: you learn with the interface and translation you understand.
home2.gD1: Memorizing the Quran by heart. Someone who has memorized it is called a hafiz.
home2.gD2: Understanding the meaning of the Quran – words, context and message.
home2.gD3: The recitation of the Quran, ideally with correct pronunciation and a calm, clear voice.
home2.gD4: The rules of pronouncing the Quranic letters and sounds correctly.
home2.gD5: A scholarly commentary that explains the verses, their context and meanings.

home2.gD10: Writing the Arabic sounds in Latin letters so that beginners can read along.
home2.q6: How long does it take to memorize a surah?
home2.a6: It depends on its length and your daily time. With 10 to 15 minutes a day, a short surah can be secured within days; the review schedule then keeps it in memory.
home2.q7: Can I use Quran Masterclass without knowing Arabic?
home2.a7: Yes. Transliteration shows how each word is read, and the translation and word-by-word meaning explain it. You learn reading and meaning together.
home2.a8: Several renowned reciters are available and more are being added. You can switch the reciter at any time.
home2.a9: We store only what is needed for your account and your learning progress, and we do not sell data. You can ask for an export or deletion at any time.
home2.q10: Does it work on my phone?
home2.a10: Yes. The site is built for phones first and works on tablets and computers in all supported languages.
home2.q11: What is the difference between tafsir and translation?
home2.a11: A translation renders the words into your language. A tafsir is a commentary by scholars that explains context, meanings and rulings.
home2.a12: Kids mode is designed for children, but we recommend that parents accompany younger learners and choose the content together.

legal.privacyBody:
## 1. Who is responsible
The operator of Quran Masterclass is responsible for processing your data. Contact details are in the imprint. Questions about your data: info@quranmasterclass.com.

## 2. What we process and why
**Account data** – first name, last name, e-mail address, country, city (optional), learning goal (optional), language, password (stored only as a salted hash), time of registration, last sign-in. Purpose: to provide your account and learning features. Legal basis: performance of the contract (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR).

**Learning data** – your progress, bookmarks, notes, review schedule and daily practice count. Purpose: to provide the learning features and to sync them across your devices. Legal basis: performance of the contract.

**E-mail for service messages** – confirmation of your address and password reset. Legal basis: performance of the contract.

**Marketing e-mails** – only if you ticked the separate box. You can withdraw consent at any time. Legal basis: consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).

**Bot protection (Google reCAPTCHA)** – to protect accounts, sign-ins, comments and feedback against automated attacks and spam we use Google reCAPTCHA on these forms (Google Ireland Limited, Gordon House, Barrow Street, Dublin 4, Ireland). reCAPTCHA is only loaded when you open such a form – not on the other pages. Technical data such as your IP address, browser information and your interaction with the page are sent to and evaluated by Google; Google may set cookies for this, and a transfer to the USA is possible. Legal basis: legitimate interest in the security of the service (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR). Google's Privacy Policy (policies.google.com/privacy) and Terms of Service (policies.google.com/terms) apply.

**Technical data and abuse protection** – to limit the free daily tafsir for visitors without an account and to protect against abuse we store, for the current day, a hashed combination of your IP address and a random cookie value, together with the verses you opened. Legal basis: legitimate interest (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

## 3. Cookies
We use only strictly necessary cookies: a session cookie after sign-in and a random identifier for the daily free-tafsir limit. We use no advertising or tracking cookies and no third-party analytics. The only exception is Google reCAPTCHA on the forms named above.

## 4. Recipients
For reCAPTCHA, Google receives the technical data named above. Our hosting provider processes data on our behalf to run the servers. If you use an e-mail feature, our e-mail provider transmits the messages. We do not sell personal data.

## 5. Storage period
Account and learning data are kept until you delete your account. Daily usage records are deleted regularly. Sessions expire after 30 days.

## 6. Your rights
You have the right to access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing, data portability and objection, and to withdraw consent at any time. Write to info@quranmasterclass.com. You may also lodge a complaint with a data protection authority.

## 7. Children
Accounts are meant for people aged 16 and over. Younger children should use the service together with a parent or guardian, who should create and manage the account.

## 8. Changes
We will update this policy when the service changes. The date above shows the latest version.

## Recitation check and recording
When you use “Recite & check”, the site uses your browser's speech recognition. Your voice is processed by the browser's provider (Google for Chrome, Apple for Safari); we only receive the recognised text in your browser and do not store it. Your own recording (“Record”) stays in your browser tab only and is never uploaded.
legal.termsBody:
## 1. Service
Quran Masterclass is an online learning service for listening to, understanding, memorizing and reciting the Quran. Basic features are free. Some features may require a free account or, later, a paid plan.

## 2. Your account
You are responsible for keeping your password confidential and for the accuracy of the data you provide. Please do not create accounts for other people without their consent.

## 3. Fair use
Do not misuse the service: no automated mass access, no attempts to bypass limits or security, no unlawful content. We may restrict accounts that violate these rules.

## 4. Content and sources
Quran text, translations and commentaries come from third-party sources and remain the property of their respective authors and publishers; they are shown with attribution. Tafsir and explanations are educational aids, not religious rulings (fatwa). For religious questions please consult a qualified scholar.

## 5. Availability and liability
We aim for reliable service but cannot guarantee uninterrupted availability. Mandatory statutory liability remains unaffected.

## 6. Changes and termination
We may change the service and these terms; we will announce material changes. You can delete your account at any time by writing to info@quranmasterclass.com.

shams.title: Shams Method
shams.recallHint: Recite from memory, then tap “Reveal” and rate yourself.
shams.d1: Listen to the verse three times with your eyes on the Arabic text. Don’t translate yet – let sound, rhythm and melody settle first.
shams.d2: The verse is built from its end: first the last word, then the last two, the last three – until the whole verse. Speak along each time. Ending on the familiar part keeps the melody natural and the verse holds together.
shams.d3: Look at each word and its meaning. Small building blocks are easier to keep than a whole sentence.
shams.d4: Read the translation of the whole verse and see how the words come together. Then use the memory hooks: the anchor word, the rhyme at the end, the bridge to the next verse – and write your own mnemonic.
shams.d5: Read the classical explanation of the verse: context, reason of revelation and what scholars teach about it. The source is shown below the text.
shams.d6: First you only see the first letter of each word – recite the verse with these cues. Then the cues disappear too. Reveal the verse and rate yourself honestly; it comes back for review at the right time.
shams.d7: Write one or two sentences in your note. Reflection (tadabbur) connects the verse to your own life – and makes it stay.
shams.q1: What does this verse tell me about Allah?
shams.q2: What does it say about me and my life?
shams.q3: What will I take with me today?
shams.pageLead: A new way to learn the Quran: seven short steps per verse that combine what language learning research knows about memory and understanding with the classical tafsir tradition.
shams.pageBy: Developed by Nami Shams in Dubai
shams.p1d: Like children learning their first language, you hear first and speak later. Repeated listening builds a sound image of the verse before you try to recite it.
shams.p2d: Teachers of long sentences in foreign languages start from the end, so that every repetition finishes on a part you already know. Quran Masterclass knows the exact moment each word is recited and can play the verse from any word to its end – that is what makes this possible.
shams.p3d: Memory holds small units more easily. Word by word, then the whole verse: the meaning is built from pieces you already know.
shams.p4d: Arabic text, sound, transliteration and meaning are connected. Several paths into memory make recall stronger.
shams.p5d: Actively recalling a verse from memory strengthens it far more than reading it again. That is why the words are hidden in step six.
shams.p6d: Each verse returns after 1, 3, 7, 14, 30 and 90 days – exactly when it is about to fade.
shams.p7d: Connecting a verse to your own life gives it meaning – and meaningful content is remembered longest.
shams.note: The Shams Method is a way of learning, not a new interpretation of the Quran. All explanations come from classical tafsir works and are shown with their source. For religious questions, please ask a qualified scholar.
shams.homeLead: Seven steps per verse – listen, shadow, words, meaning, tafsir, recall, reflect. Developed by Nami Shams from language learning research.
shams.dayTitle: Your day with the Shams Method
shams.dayLead: Fifteen to twenty-five focused minutes a day beat a long session once a week. Every day has the same four parts:
shams.day1d: Start with the verses that are due today. Recalling them from memory before you learn anything new is what moves them into long-term memory.
shams.day2t: New verses in seven steps (about 4 min per verse)
shams.day2d: Take your daily portion – for most people three new verses – through listen, shadow, words, meaning, tafsir, recall and reflect.
shams.day3d: Recite today’s new verses together with yesterday’s, without looking. This links verses into a passage, as the classical hifz teachers do with sabaq and sabqi.
shams.day4d: Play today’s verses once more in the evening. What you go over shortly before sleep is consolidated overnight.
shams.howLead: The right amount is the one you can keep up every day. Our recommendation:
shams.how3: Intensive: 5–10 new verses plus a longer review
shams.howNote: Reviews grow with every verse you learn, so a steady small portion is better than a big start you cannot keep.
shams.newP1: Many apps play a verse and show a translation. The Shams Method uses what only a platform with exact word timings can do: it builds every verse up backwards from its last word, and it fades the text out in stages – from the full verse to first letters to nothing. Together with listening first, word-by-word meaning, classical tafsir, spaced review and reflection, this becomes one fixed path per verse.
shams.newP2: The building blocks come from language learning and memory research and from the hifz tradition – that is what makes them reliable. New is how they are combined and put into practice step by step, for every verse of the Quran, in about four minutes.
shams.planNote: Estimate for learning new verses every day, including daily review. Learning speed differs from person to person – what counts is that you stay with it.
shams.chainDone: Whole verse built up – well done.
shams.cueHint: Recite with the first letters as cues.
shams.p8d: Memory research uses cues that are gradually taken away. Seeing only the first letter of each word is just enough help to recall the word yourself – then the help disappears.

shams.fa1: A seven-step method developed by Nami Shams for learning the Holy Quran online: listen, build up backwards, word by word, meaning, tafsir, fading cues and reflection. It is free at Quran Masterclass.
shams.fq2: How many verses should I learn per day?
shams.fa2: For beginners one to three new verses a day plus the review that is due. With practice three to five. The amount you can keep up every day is the right one.
shams.fq3: Do I need to know Arabic?
shams.fa3: No. Transliteration and word-by-word meaning help you from the first verse. Over time you recognise words and letters on your own.
shams.fq4: Is the Shams Method a new tafsir?
shams.fa4: No. It is a learning method. Explanations come from classical tafsir works and are shown with their source.

shams.hOwnPh: A picture, a story, a link to your life …
shams.p9t: A memory model that learns you
shams.p9d: Like an intelligent tutor, the platform learns how your memory works: every verse gets its own memory factor. It drops when you struggle and grows when a verse comes easily, every mistake in a test brings the verse back the next day, and your weakest verses are shown first. No two learners get the same schedule.
shams.p10d: Language learners remember words with images and stories. For the Quran, the strongest hooks are already in the text: the anchor word of a verse, the rhyme at its end (many verses of a surah end the same way), and the bridge from the last word of one verse to the first word of the next – the point where most people get stuck.
shams.whyTitle: Why learning the Quran matters more than anything
shams.whyLead: For a believing Muslim, the Quran is the word of Allah – the guide for life and the companion in the grave and on the Day of Judgement. The Prophet ﷺ placed learning it above everything else:
shams.why1: “The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.”
shams.why2: “Read the Quran, for it will come on the Day of Resurrection as an intercessor for its companions.”
shams.why3: “Whoever reads a letter from the Book of Allah receives a good deed, and every good deed is multiplied by ten.”
shams.why4: “The one who recites the Quran skilfully will be with the noble, righteous scribes, and the one who recites it with difficulty, stumbling over it, receives a double reward.”
shams.why5: “And We have certainly made the Quran easy for remembrance – so is there anyone who will remember?”
shams.whyClose: That is why Quran Masterclass is free – and why the Shams Method exists: so that nobody has to postpone the most important learning of their life.

plan.about:
## Why the amount grows
Memory is like a muscle: it grows with steady, slightly increasing load. That is why every track starts with a portion you can manage easily and adds a little more every week. Intensive Quran schools work the same way – small at first, more every week, and daily review of everything learned so far.

## The five daily tasks
1. **Review first** – the verses your memory model marks as due.
2. **New verses** – in seven steps with the Shams Method.
3. **Chain** – today's and yesterday's verses together, so they grow into a passage.
4. **Test** – the Academy test on time shows what really sits.
5. **Evening** – listen once more before sleep.

## Which track is right?
- **Gentle** for beginners and children: from one verse a day.
- **Standard** for most adults with job and family.
- **Intensive** for those who want to make fast progress.
- **Hafiz track** for full-time students: about two pages a day at the top, the whole Quran in about one year – best together with a teacher you recite to.

If you fall behind, the plan shows your backlog. Catch up before adding more – quality before speed.

about.lead: Quran Masterclass is a free platform to listen to, understand, memorise and recite the Quran – in 13 languages, for children and adults, wherever they live.
about.seoTitle: About Quran Masterclass – free Quran learning, made in Dubai
about.seoDesc: Quran Masterclass was founded by Nami Shams in Dubai: a free platform to learn the Quran with the Shams Method, in 13 languages. Our mission, values and team.
about.body:
## Our mission
The best of people, the Prophet ﷺ said, are those who learn the Quran and teach it. We want to make that possible for everyone – without fees, without ads, without a teacher nearby being the only way in. Learning the Quran should be as natural as using your phone every day.

## How it started
Quran Masterclass was founded by **Nami Shams** in Dubai. The question was simple: why do language apps help millions learn every day, while learning the Quran often stays a plan for later? The answer became the [Shams Method](/shams) – seven steps per verse that combine what memory research knows with the way Quran teachers have always taught.

## What we believe
- **Free for everyone.** The Quran belongs to every Muslim. Voluntary support keeps the platform running.
- **Authentic sources.** Quran text, translations and tafsir come from recognised sources and always show where they come from. We do not create new interpretations.
- **Respect.** No ads, no tracking, no selling of data. Comments are reviewed before they appear.
- **For every age.** From children's first surah to the hafiz track – the method adapts to you.

## Get in touch
Write to info@quranmasterclass.com or send a request on our [feedback page](/feedback).

trust.how:
All connections are encrypted with HTTPS.
Passwords are never stored in plain text, only as a salted scrypt hash.
Every account must be confirmed through an e-mail link.
Bot protection (Google reCAPTCHA) on sign-in, sign-up, comments and feedback.
Lock-out after too many wrong passwords – per account and per IP address.
Strict security headers (Content Security Policy) against injected scripts.
No ads, no analytics services, no selling of data.
Comments and feedback are reviewed before they appear.
Data export and account deletion any time in your profile.

duagen.metaDesc: Choose your concern and receive a personal dua with the fitting names of Allah – together with the authentic duas of the Quran and the Sunnah, with sources.
duagen.title: Your dua – in your own words
duagen.lead: Choose what is on your heart, write it in your own words and say who you are praying for. We put your dua together the way the Prophet ﷺ taught: with praise of Allah, blessings on the Prophet, the fitting beautiful names of Allah – and with the real duas of the Quran and the Sunnah.
duagen.placeholder: For example: my exam is tomorrow and I am anxious …
duagen.anyLanguage: You can pray to Allah in any language.
duagen.praiseTr: All praise is for Allah, Lord of the worlds.
duagen.salawatTr: O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and the family of Muhammad.
duagen.closeTr: Our Lord, give us good in this world and good in the Hereafter, and protect us from the punishment of the Fire.
duagen.forWho: I ask You for all of this {who} as well.
duagen.aiLogin: For more phrasings please sign up for free.
duagen.aiLimit: Today's limit is reached – more tomorrow.
duagen.aiError: That did not work just now. Your dua above stays as it is.
duagen.note: The part in your own words is a personal dua – not a Quran or hadith text. Arabic lines: Quran 1:2 and 2:201 and the blessing from the prayer (al-Bukhari 3370).
duagen.time1: In the last third of the night
duagen.time1d: Allah asks: who is calling upon Me, that I may answer him? (al-Bukhari 1145, Muslim 758)
duagen.time2d: The servant is closest to his Lord when he prostrates, so make much dua then. (Muslim 482)
duagen.time3d: The dua between the call to prayer and the iqamah is not rejected. (Abu Dawud 521, at-Tirmidhi 212)
duagen.time4d: On Friday there is an hour in which Allah grants every good request. (al-Bukhari 935, Muslim 852)
duagen.time5d: Three duas are answered without doubt: that of the parent, the traveller and the one who is wronged. (Abu Dawud 1536, at-Tirmidhi 1905)
duagen.adab1: Begin with praise of Allah and blessings on the Prophet ﷺ, then ask. (at-Tirmidhi 3477, Abu Dawud 1481)
duagen.adab2: Pray with certainty that Allah will answer. (at-Tirmidhi 3479)
duagen.adab3: Be patient – do not say: I prayed and was not answered. (al-Bukhari 6340, Muslim 2735)
duagen.adab4: Pray for others in their absence – an angel says: and for you the same. (Muslim 2732)
duagen.req_worry: O Allah, lift the worry from my heart and let me find peace in remembering You. You know what weighs on me before I say it. Make the way easy for me and give me trust in You – You are enough for me.
duagen.req_illness: O Allah, You are the Healer. Grant me complete healing, take the pain away from me, give me strength in body and patience in heart, and let this time bring me closer to You.
duagen.req_knowledge: O Allah, open my understanding, make learning easy for me and let me keep what I have learned. Give me calm in the exam, a clear mind and beneficial knowledge that serves me and others.
duagen.req_forgiveness: O Allah, I have wronged myself. Forgive me my sins, the great and the small, the known and the hidden. Accept my repentance and help me to become better – You are the Forgiving, the Merciful.
duagen.req_parents: O Allah, have mercy on my parents as they raised me when I was small. Grant them health, a long good life and Your forgiveness, and help me to do good to them.
duagen.req_children: O Allah, bless my children and make them a comfort to my eyes. Protect them, guide them on the straight path and let them love the Quran.
duagen.req_marriage: O Allah, bless my marriage – or grant me a good spouse if I am still alone. Put love and mercy between us and make our home a place of peace and of Your remembrance.
duagen.req_provision: O Allah, grant me abundant, good and lawful provision, open the doors of good for me and bless my work. Let me be content with what is lawful and free me from debt.
duagen.req_guidance: O Allah, show me what is right and help me to follow it. If this matter is good for my faith, my life and my end, then decree it for me and make it easy; if not, keep it away from me and decree the good for me wherever it is.
duagen.req_travel: O Allah, be with me on this journey, make the way easy and the distance short. Protect me and everyone I leave behind, and bring me back safely.
duagen.req_protection: O Allah, protect me from every evil that I see and that I do not see, from envy and from the evil eye. I place myself, my family and everything You have given me under Your protection.
duagen.req_gratitude: O Allah, all praise is Yours for Your countless gifts. Help me to thank You and to remember You, and let me use Your gifts in the way that pleases You.
duagen.req_deceased: O Allah, forgive the one who has passed away and have mercy on them, make their grave wide and full of light, reunite us in Paradise and comfort all who grieve.
duagen.req_heart: O Allah, make my heart firm in Your faith, make the Quran the spring of my heart and the light of my chest. Purify my intention and let me love You and all that brings me closer to You.
duagen.nd_latif: He knows the finest things and guides them with kindness, often in ways we do not see.
duagen.nd_salam: Free of every flaw, He gives peace and safety.
duagen.nd_wakil: Whoever entrusts his affairs to Him, He is enough for him.
duagen.nd_shafi: Healing comes from Him – this is how the Prophet ﷺ called on Him (al-Bukhari 5675).
duagen.nd_rahim: He has mercy on those who come to Him.
duagen.nd_alim: Nothing is hidden from Him – He knows what you need.
duagen.nd_fattah: He opens the doors of knowledge, provision and mercy.
duagen.nd_hakim: There is wisdom in everything He decrees.
duagen.nd_tawwab: He turns to whoever turns to Him.
duagen.nd_afuww: He erases mistakes as if they had never been.
duagen.nd_barr: The source of all that is good.
duagen.nd_wahhab: He gives without return and without limit.
duagen.nd_hafiz: He keeps and guards what is entrusted to Him.
duagen.nd_wadud: He loves His servants and places love in hearts.
duagen.nd_karim: He gives abundantly, even when we do not deserve it.
duagen.nd_hadi: He guides hearts to what is right.
duagen.nd_hamid: All praise is His, in every state.
duagen.ownWords: O Allah, You know what is on my heart: “{text}”

donate.kicker: Sadaqa for the Word of Allah
donate.title: Quran Masterclass stays free – with your help
donate.lead: No fees, no subscription, no ads. Servers, recitations, development and new courses are carried by voluntary donations alone. If you can and wish to, help this project grow – for everyone who wants to learn and understand the Word of Allah and, in sha Allah, recite it beautifully one day.
donate.free: Donations are voluntary. Everything stays free for everyone – with or without a donation.
donate.slimTitle: This project lives on voluntary donations.
donate.slimLead: If you can, help – every gift opens the way to the Quran for others.
donate.s1: When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: an ongoing charity, knowledge that benefits, or a righteous child who prays for him.
donate.s3: The best of you are those who learn the Quran and teach it.
donate.s4: Whoever guides someone to good has a reward like the one who does it.
donate.s5: Allah says: Spend, O son of Adam, and I will spend on you.
